headline: Major US banks are restricting external AI agent access, Axios reports
body: Several major US banks, including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America and Wells Fargo, are restricting external AI agent access, according to Axios. Most want to limit agents to read-only access, letting them view account data but not carry out any actions.
note: Many banks also can’t tell whether an agent is acting on a user’s behalf, and The Decoder says blocking agents on the provider side will be hard.

evidence.text: Several major US banks, including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo, are restricting external AI agent access, Axios reports .
Most banks want to limit agents to read-only access, letting them view account data but not carry out any actions.
Many banks also can't tell whether an agent is acting on a user's behalf or accessing an account on its own.
Blocking that on the provider side will be hard.
